_nota: Frasi della card 'Scritto a mano' del sabato (pagina 3 del modello Canva). Lista separata dai mantra, usata in ordine: una a settimana, mai due volte la stessa. La n. 1 è quella già scritta nel modello da Paolo. La routine aggiorna 'usati' a ogni uscita. Dal 20 ottobre 2026 il testo è in INGLESE (richiesta di Paolo): stessa numerazione, quelli già usciti sono usciti in italiano.
frasi: I still remember going to school and taking notes with... my hands.
I remember when leaving a message on the fridge… meant walking to the kitchen.
Back then, autocorrect was the teacher. And she took it very seriously.
I miss when a letter began with “Dear”. And someone had actually thought about you.
Before sending a heart… we tried drawing one.
Back then, you knew “typing…” from the sound of the pen.
I miss when deleting a word… meant leaving a trace.
I remember when my notes were in my own handwriting. Unfortunately.
Back then, love letters had mistakes. But they were all ours.
I miss when a signature looked like someone.
Back then, the voice message was my mother at the window. Perfect coverage.
I remember when finding your friends… meant looking for the bikes outside.
Before sharing your location… we said “I'm downstairs”.
Back then, “follow me” was a friend who knew a shortcut.
I miss when “did you arrive?” was a phone call. With someone waiting.
I remember when we rang doorbells without booking the friendship first.
Back then, to know how you were… I had to listen to the answer.
I miss when “seen” meant we had actually looked at each other.
I remember when the family group chat… was everyone around one table.
Back then, “sending you a kiss” was a promise with uncertain delivery times.
I miss when making a good impression… meant showing up.
Back then, photos came out blurry. But we were really there.
I remember when to see a photo… we had to finish the holiday first.
I miss when the album had little corner mounts. And someone always cut out.
Back then, the photo filter was a finger over the lens.
I remember when a bad photo was kept. Because it came from a good day.
I miss when to zoom in on a photo… we all leaned closer.
Back then, memories fit in a box. That nobody had the heart to throw away.
I remember when a playlist for someone… took a cassette and a bit of courage.
Back then, to hear a song again… we had to rewind our impatience too.
I miss when a dedication on the radio… could fix your whole day.
I remember when the record skipped. And we knew exactly where.
Back then, recommended music was “listen to this”. And we knew who was telling us.
I miss when a recipe had a sauce stain. That was the review.
Back then, “as much as needed” was decided by grandma. No updates.
I remember when good morning… sounded like coffee cups.
I miss when cakes were crooked. And nobody asked to regenerate them.
Back then, to personalise a gift… you just had to think of someone.
I remember when handmade things… carried a bit of whoever made them.
I miss when the sweater itched. But grandma had made it.
Back then, the instructions were “watch how I do it”. And two hands close by.
I remember when “ask someone”… assumed there was someone.
Back then, the search engine was my father. Even when he didn't know the answer.
I miss when to translate a sentence… we looked up one word at a time. Even the love ones.
I remember when we got lost. And came back with something to tell.
Back then, the suggested route was “come this way, I'll buy you a coffee”.
I miss when an answer came after a “let me think”. And I could see the face.
I remember when to get an idea… we doodled until the page gave up.
Back then, “made by me” needed no explanation.
I miss when a surprise… didn't already know what I liked.
I remember when we wrote “sorry about my handwriting”. As if leaving something of ourselves were a flaw.
